agent.problem: Five of the nine choice cards (3, 5, 8, 10 and 17) require unseen details that cannot be reasoned from the earlier cards: whether the word continues after Josiah, the exile, the nations, Jeremiah's objection and the rest of the job list. That leaves only four informed guesses, so most of this stop's choices are discoveries rather than informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Verse 10 is reduced to an unnamed job list. Neither this card nor card 17 supplies the list, so the baker misses uprooting, tearing down, destroying and overthrowing, followed by building and planting. The true-or-false question only establishes that the work is not exclusively destructive.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: Nothing before this card indicates the pot's direction, so north is an unseen word chosen by luck from three directions rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The setup says only that the northern kings are coming. It gives no basis for choosing gates rather than the temple or palace, so this blank asks the baker to guess an unseen detail.

agent.problem: The claim that Jeremiah goes from only a child to like an iron pillar in one conversation adds a timeframe the passage never gives. The call and the two visions are introduced by separate comings of the word of the LORD, with no statement that everything occurs in one conversation.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.
